description: OptiGob is a Python model for exploring agriculture, forestry and other land-use transitions in Ireland. Its developers combine output from GOBLIN Lite, FERS-CBM and LCAD2.0 with pathway assumptions to calculate environmental and economic measures. The own README names land area, emissions, protein output, bioenergy and harvested wood among results. Spatial coverage is Ireland and the supplied land units; temporal period and resolution follow the scenario settings and linked model outputs. The public repository reports MIT, so the code is free. A food-supply or bioenergy modeller can compare land allocation and emissions pathways before using them in wider system scenarios. A caveat is that linked model uncertainty and biophysical constraints govern the result; a feasible model allocation is not a funded or approved land-use change. Results should not be transferred to another country without rebuilding input assumptions. No directly related catalogue record was found. The article and own repository were read without running a pathway.
